title: ask-the-brain
universal_lens: The Ask-the-Brain architecture formalizes a constrained epistemic manifold where natural language queries map to structured evidence vectors. By enforcing strict confidence bounds and explicit weakening signals, the system operates as a rigorous projection operator, ensuring that all generated intelligence remains strictly bounded by the underlying evidentiary subspace.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, Brain answers function as posterior distributions derived from hierarchical Bayesian inference over multi-tiered source graphs. The explicit confidence levels and required weakening conditions directly map to conformal prediction sets, guaranteeing finite-sample coverage while dynamically adjusting for the decay of information freshness across the entity graph.
gse_mapping: For GSE, the Brain acts as a continuous state-transition evaluator within the situational reasoning engine. Evidence updates trigger discrete jumps in the Markovian state space of team/player dynamics, allowing the engine to re-evaluate tactical schemes and injury rehabilitation trajectories without hallucinating unobserved latent variables.

primitives.name: Evidence Projection Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: No Brain answer fabricates data or implies certainty it cannot support.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: A: Answer vector (dimensionless), E: Evidence subspace (dimensionless), P_E: Orthogonal projection operator onto E.
primitives.assumptions: The evidentiary subspace E is well-defined and retrievable; the projection operator P_E is idempotent and Hermitian.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the evidence subspace E becomes empty or highly degenerate, forcing the system into an undefined null-state rather than hallucinating.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the strict constraint enforcement in GSI's conformal inference, where predictions are explicitly truncated at the boundary of the observed calibration set.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of 'cockpit-only' flags triggered due to insufficient Tier-1 through Tier-4 evidence.

primitives.name: Epistemic Uncertainty Quantifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: It produces structured, evidence-cited answers to sports intelligence questions for operators and, eventually, premium users.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C: Confidence level (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, ordinal dimensionless), S_w: Weakening signal set (boolean/dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Uncertainty can be discretized into actionable ordinal buckets; weakening signals are logically independent of the primary assertion.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails under adversarial prompt injection designed to force a HIGH confidence rating on contradictory or stale evidence.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the variance estimation kernel in GSE's situational reasoning, providing the error bars required for robust Monte Carlo simulations of game states.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of confidence ratings across identical query permutations; frequency of LOW confidence overrides.

primitives.name: Temporal Decay Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: // Full implementation requires Evidence Vault, Entity Graph, and Signal // Ledger to be in place.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: Current time (seconds), t_0: Evidence retrieval time (seconds), \tau: Staleness threshold (seconds).
primitives.assumptions: Information value decays monotonically with time delta \Delta t = t - t_0; the Entity Graph accurately reflects current physical realities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur during sudden, unlogged regime shifts (e.g., surprise IR placements) where the Signal Ledger has not yet updated.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the state-refresh triggers in GSE, ensuring that tactical evaluations are only computed on non-stale manifolds defined by the Entity Graph.
layer2.telemetry: Latency between real-world event occurrence and Signal Ledger update; percentage of answers flagged as staleAt.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Ask-the-Brain doctrine establishes a rigorous mathematical framework for converting unstructured sports intelligence queries into bounded, evidence-backed assertions. The core operator is the Evidence Projection Operator, which ensures that any generated answer A lies strictly within the span of the retrieved evidence subspace E. This prevents hallucination by mathematically forbidding extrapolation beyond the observed data manifold. Complementing this is the Epistemic Uncertainty Quantifier, which assigns an ordinal confidence level C and a set of weakening signals S_w to every projection. This dual-output structure mirrors conformal prediction, providing both a point estimate (the direct answer) and a validity region (confidence/weakening conditions). The Temporal Decay Gate further constrains the system by mapping the Entity Graph's timestamps to a staleness metric, effectively zeroing out the influence of evidence vectors that exceed a predefined temporal threshold \tau. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop epistemic system where the launch sequence acts as a progressive relaxation of constraints, moving from a highly restricted internal cockpit (strict projection, manual review) to a public beta (automated governance, visible uncertainty). The failure modes of this system are precisely defined: it breaks down when the evidence subspace is empty (yielding no answer rather than a false one) or when the temporal decay gate fails to capture rapid regime shifts in the underlying sports ontology.

Across Galaxy Sports Intelligence (GSI) and Galaxy Sports Engine (GSE), strict mathematical isomorphism separates immutable source invariants from downstream derived kernels. Whenever empirical estimates depend on finite-sample observation windows, James-Stein / Empirical-Bayes shrinkage pulls noisy displacement signals back toward hierarchical priors while censoring extreme displacements within +/- 0.35 log-odds. Weighted conformal calibration further ensures distribution-free finite-sample coverage even under covariate shift between historical training splits and live operational weeks. Crucially, zero-leakage chronological causality demands that every parameter, variance weight, and situational adjustment strictly precede the target event horizon, preventing forward leakage or post-hoc optimization bias. reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This architecture inherits deeply from the Frechet-Kolmogorov foundations of probability theory, specifically the axiomatization of belief under incomplete information. It also draws from modern conformal inference (Vovk et al.), which provides distribution-free uncertainty quantification, and knowledge graph embedding theories that map entities to vector spaces. The requirement for explicit weakening signals echoes the philosophical tradition of falsifiability established by Popper, translated here into a computational constraint.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The system models the user (operator or premium subscriber) as an agent seeking to minimize decision risk under uncertainty. By explicitly providing confidence levels and weakening conditions, the Brain anticipates the user's need to stress-test the intelligence against their own priors. It also models opposing agents (e.g., sportsbooks, rival teams) by tracking how external signals (like prop line moves) alter the evidentiary landscape, treating market movements as noisy observations of hidden states.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists between the Brain's output and Component 1 (Picks Intelligence). The Brain is strictly forbidden from producing direct pick recommendations; it only supplies the evidentiary substrate. This anti-collinearity veto prevents the conflation of factual inference with strategic optimization. Furthermore, any answer relying solely on Tier-5 evidence (unverified rumors) is automatically vetoed from public surfaces, acting as a hard filter against low-signal noise leaking into the high-stakes decision layers of GSE.
